subject: Explicit replication: independent proposal, CLI and native dispatch consumers review

author.role: Independent production reviewer and author of three new test files; not a B3 production author

production_owners.core_review: Persistent request store and request service
production_owners.runtime_evidence: Independent execution slots and native launch/cleanup binding

scope.implemented_by_others: Explicit durable request admits a distinct task with the original raw configuration and semantic execution/artifact specification. Ordinary proposal dedup remains authoritative for accidental duplication.
scope.tested: Actual Pro research cycle and source append; actual Core CLI/project loader/request service/empty source sync/training dispatch/claim/native terminal/artifact occurrence. Provider and OS/GPU boundaries are test doubles; no paid provider, actual GPU or holdout.
not_claimed: Scientific independence or improved research results from identical specification/seed
Observation aggregation, automatic best-of-repeats or statistical comparability
Third-party extension compatibility: an additional external duplicate veto can still reject a replica
Arbitrary SQL or hostile filesystem tamperproofing
Interrupted native checkpoint resume or permission to replay open/uncertain attempts
scope.conclusion: No remaining blocker found in the bounded B3 default/native contract after the final local CLI configuration fix.

coverage: Exact reserved config fields replication_request_id and replication_authorization, recursively, including False and None, cannot increase the cycle's accepted count.
Mixed forged/ordinary batch retains exactly the legitimate proposal and partial status.
Same-config repeat and top-level authored request metadata do not bypass ordinary proposal dedup.
Legacy replication_role/index remain ordinary data: an appended proposal does not become a new durable task when Core ordinary config dedup applies.

Two actual CLI requests from outside project cwd admit distinct tasks; an empty proposal source still reaches real sync, training dispatch and claim. Same raw config/seed, semantic execution identity and artifact specification; distinct attempt/artifact occurrence IDs and physical paths; original source owner/row/artifacts unchanged.
Same-key CLI replay while the child is RUNNING returns its original task, does not reset state/claim, and does not launch a duplicate process.
Nonempty YAML list, malformed YAML, False and empty list return int 2 plus one JSON error before database opening or request service entry; existing DB/file bytes and cwd remain unchanged.
own_frozen_tests.fixture_scope: Real main/parser/project loader; root CLI boundary fixture mocks the request service only, and an opener tripwire asserts no authority access for malformed input.

shared_B3_inventory.attribution: Cross-checked against root's per-file inventory; scope-empty is the fourth control. Draft failures are scope 1, nullable category 1, slot recovery 2 and CLI config 4. This is not a sum of test run totals.
shared_B3_inventory.excluded: Ordinary both-None native authorization compatibility used one pre-existing public test and therefore does not increase the 64 new tests.

counting.overlapping_run_policy: 102/36/15/32 and subsequent reruns overlap; they are separate source-epoch checks, never added as distinct coverage.

fixture_and_evidence_corrections: A first Pro working-tree run was 4 failed / 3 passed in 1.83s during concurrent preflight authoring; only the later fixed-module 1.33s replay is used as the official baseline.

The first native dispatch draft (SHA 245e0fe663d2cd3552c24254ef5be176bc60ad76c0cb3f863b949123fa3fca1b) encountered two setup errors in 0.90s because the production draft rejected canonical_identity_equal(None, None). The runtime author independently froze an existing normal-launch regression and fixed the both-None branch. Those setup errors are not additional CLI public reds.

The next native dispatch draft run had two failures in 1.19s because its manually assembled source configuration differed from the real CLI loader defaults. replication_execution_inputs_changed was a correct rejection. The fixture was corrected to load the real source configuration before launch, preserving the business assertions. No pre-existing frozen test was changed.
No import absence is classified as a historical product bug. No unfinished fixture draft is treated as a frozen old-source snapshot.

Root's interrupted candidate Core/Pro full suites, including pytest temporary-directory teardown KeyError, are excluded from this review's product-red evidence. Full-suite execution and final inventory belong to root, not this reviewer.
independent_review: Durable request records authorize only an exact current confirmed source and immutable subject/config/execution/artifact bindings. Request replay reads back the same mapping rather than creating another task.
Exact config key presence for idea_lake_db is respected through the shared resolver, including explicit None/default selection; a foreign supplied lake cannot silently override it.
Native request ownership is revalidated at actual claim/launch. Replica execution slots do not replace the original flat ordinary owner; file identity, not matching bytes alone, fences cleanup.

Confirmed closed requeued/failed/not-started attempts may retry the same requested occurrence; open, completed and uncertain states are not blindly reset. Interrupted checkpoint restoration remains separately unsupported.

Pro proposal metadata is not replication authority. Exact reserved fields are rejected, but legacy replication_role/index and domain replication_factor remain ordinary data. Accepted proposal count is not a count of newly admitted tasks.

Final CLI change is local YAML top-level prevalidation and specific YAML/type error handling. It does not catch arbitrary exceptions or modify the global project loader, and all four malformed-input cases stop before authority access.
The explicit-replication contract distinguishes independently recorded occurrences from scientific independence and acknowledges external policy vetoes.
